summary: Luke Badiali reviewed revenue operations with Andrew Fenwick and Kate Rowley. Elmstead runs pipeline in a spreadsheet alongside an underused CRM with 8 licences. We agreed to make the CRM the single source of truth for the six-stage pipeline from week 5 and to introduce a monthly forecast with commit and best-case figures.

discussion.keyPoints: Andrew confirmed 8 CRM licences, mostly unused, with the real pipeline held in Kate's spreadsheet. Partners log almost nothing about pre-tender conversations.
The board receives a single pipeline total each month. Luke suggested splitting commit and best case so the lumpy tender timing is visible. Andrew agreed the board would welcome it.
Kate raised that contact data for change directors is out of date and many records lack the organisation's regulator.

recommendations.recommendation: Retire the pipeline spreadsheet by the end of next month and run all six stages in the existing CRM, extending licences from 8 to 15.
Present a monthly forecast to the board with commit, best case and pipeline columns, with commit only from Preferred bidder stage.
Add a mandatory regulator field and a last-contact date to every account record.
Build one partner dashboard showing pre-tender conversations against the 20 per quarter target.
Write a full sales playbook for each segment this quarter.

actions.action: Migrate the spreadsheet pipeline into the CRM

nextFocus: Align marketing campaigns with the regulatory-pressure narrative and the partner outbound programme.
nextPreparation: Kate to bring the last 12 months of marketing activity and spend.

tests.question: How many CRM licences are we moving to?
Is the mandatory regulator field agreed?
Which stage counts towards commit in the forecast?
